subject.title: feat(agents): agent-controlled session status, attention, and TTL in the sessions tool

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose agent-controlled `statusNote`, `attention`, and `ttlMinutes` through the core model-facing `sessions` tool and persist the resulting status on session entries?
rationale: This is a new agent capability and persistent session contract rather than a repair to established behavior; the implementation can be sound while the permanent product boundary still requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve the bounded core contract
options.body: Keep the three fields, curated icon set, 120-minute cap, and existing read/reply/expiry clearing semantics after live proof is added.

options.title: Narrow the feature
options.body: Keep transient status text but remove or revise the persistent attention/TTL controls if maintainers want a smaller model-facing session API.

options.title: Defer the capability
options.body: Pause the PR if session presence should instead be derived automatically or designed through a broader agent-status product discussion.

recommendation.title: Approve the bounded core contract
recommendation.body: Keep the three fields, curated icon set, 120-minute cap, and existing read/reply/expiry clearing semantics after live proof is added.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged sidebar attention and narration features this proposal directly builds on.
